footerNote: Coinbase reports no gross-profit line; 'Transaction expense' — the direct cost of processing trades — is shown as cost of revenue. Coinbase also reports two lines inside operating expenses that the chart shows in the 'other income' step instead: a $31M loss on crypto held for operations and $34M of other operating expense — $65M in total. In Q2 those lines were expenses rather than the gains seen in Q3 and Q4 2024, so the chart's operating profit is $409M rather than the reported $343M — net income is unchanged. Figures are from Coinbase's Q2 2024 shareholder letter (Exhibit 99.1) and Form 10-Q.

otherDetail: A $319M loss on crypto Coinbase holds as an investment, $64M of other expense (losses on crypto loan receivables, other financial instruments and strategic investments), $21M of interest expense, and the $65M of operating losses moved here from operating expenses (a $31M loss on crypto held for operations and $34M of other operating expense — see footer): a net $469M expense.

takeaways.text: Transaction revenue rose 139% year over year to $781M — consumer trading alone was $665M — even though volume fell 28% from Q1 to $226B as crypto volatility eased from the ETF-launch peak.
takeaways.title: Trading more than doubled from a year ago

takeaways.text: Subscription and services revenue rose 79% year over year to $599M — 41% of all revenue — led by stablecoin revenue of $240M and blockchain rewards of $185M. It grew 17% from Q1 even as trading fell.
takeaways.title: Steadier revenue kept diversifying

takeaways.text: A $319M pre-tax loss on crypto Coinbase holds as an investment — the vast majority unrealized, $248M after tax — plus a $96M tax benefit left net income at just $36M, even though Adjusted EBITDA was $596M for a 6th straight positive quarter.
takeaways.title: Paper crypto losses capped profit

verdict: Coinbase's revenue more than doubled from a year ago to $1.45B as trading revenue surged, but a $319M paper loss on the crypto it holds as an investment held net income to just $36M.
